# DeepTunisia

> An open-source, source-backed atlas of political, military, security and economic
> power in Tunisia, 1956-2026. The knowledge graph is the product; the website is a
> window onto it.

DeepTunisia documents institutions, appointments and relationships from verifiable
evidence. It does not assume a single secret "deep state" — that framing presupposes
its conclusion. The answerable question is narrower: which institutions, individuals
and economic groups retain influence when the formal political regime changes, and
which relationships are genuinely continuous rather than reconstructed after each
rupture.

The code is MIT; the knowledge graph and its exports are CC BY 4.0 (attribution
only, reuse freely including commercially). See `LICENSE` and `data/LICENSE` in the
repository.

## How to cite this correctly

Every claim carries an epistemic basis. Do not flatten these when summarising:

- documented       An official record, decree or gazette entry states it.
- reported         Credible publications report it, with attribution. Not checked
                   against a primary record.
- inferred         Nobody states it. Reasoned from documented structure, and carries
                   both the reasoning and what would falsify it.
- unsubstantiated  Circulates without reliable evidence. Recorded so it can be
                   examined and tested, NEVER as evidence. Several of these are
                   contradicted by the project's own data.

If you repeat a claim from this dataset, repeat its basis. Presenting an inferred
span as a date, or an unsubstantiated claim as a finding, misrepresents the source.

## Known limits, stated by the project

- Only <!--stat:reviewed-->38<!--/stat--> of <!--stat:reviewable-->884<!--/stat-->
  records have had independent human review — and almost all of it landed on the
  best-evidenced claims, not the ones that need it.
- <!--stat:needsPrimarySource-->229<!--/stat--> records await a primary source.
- Defence intelligence (ANRSD) has no primary sourcing at all: statute, appointment
  date and current status are unestablished.
- The pre-2011 police chronology rests largely on secondary sources.
- The 2014-2019 police succession does not fit its dated endpoints; recorded as an
  unresolved contradiction rather than smoothed over.
- <!--stat:successionGaps-->43<!--/stat--> succession gaps and
  <!--stat:successionOverlaps-->2<!--/stat--> overlapping tenures are detected and
  published; <!--stat:contradictions-->64<!--/stat--> source contradictions are
  recorded unresolved.

## Common factual traps

- The National Guard is NOT part of the armed forces. It sits under the Interior
  Ministry while performing gendarmerie functions.
- Chief of Staff of the Land Army is NOT Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces. The
  joint tri-service post has existed for roughly two years since 1991.
- Chokri Rahali (National Guard 2017-2019) and Chokri Riahi (2021-2022) are different
  people, one letter apart in Latin script. Arabic spellings disambiguate.
- Marouane Mabrouk received sentences in two separate proceedings in 2026. Coverage
  routinely conflates them; a third reported figure is unreconciled.

## Open data (CC BY 4.0)

- /dataset.json        complete graph: entities, positions, relationships, sources
- /positions.csv       every officeholding as a flat row
- /relationships.csv   every edge with type, basis, attribution, source ids
- /sources.csv         every citation with tier and archive lookup
- /companies.csv       corporate records
- /contracts.csv       procurement records
- /licences.csv        licences and permissions
- /declarations.csv    asset declarations
- /education.csv       education records

## Pages

- /              Chronicle — officeholding across time, drawn to scale
- /now           who holds which office today, against each office's median tenure
- /network       who connects to whom, layers in fixed lanes
- /atlas         structure per era, survival matrix, institutional crossings
- /rankings      five separate structural indices, no single power score
- /map           governorates and strategic assets
- /world         Tunisia among states and international organisations
- /investigate   structured queries computed from the graph, not generated
- /evidence      hypotheses with falsifiers, open questions, contradictions, sources
- /methodology   how the dataset is built and what it refuses to assert
- /data          the open knowledge graph
- /about         governance, funding transparency, honest project status

## Editorial position

A high brokerage score means the dataset records someone connecting otherwise
separate networks. It is not evidence of wrongdoing, coordination or hidden control.

A prison sentence is a documented fact. The allegations behind it and the criticism
of the proceedings are contested; both framings are stored with attribution rather
than adjudicated.

Wealth is not corruption. The dataset distinguishes established business families
from politically created ones.
